analysis.headline: Perfect recall. All 7 gold files across all 4 gold repos returned, with the three anchor defect files ranked 1-3 and every contract-owner citation found. The cost is precision: 18 of 25 returned paths are not gold.
what_worked: The anchor was nailed and ranked first. TLFileDurableObject.ts, publishSnapshots.ts and r2.ts - the exact three files of PR #10298 - occupy ranks 1, 2 and 3 with nothing non-gold between them.

All three contract-owner citations were resolved from prose alone, in three different repos: RTK's entity adapters for 'one mutator for single, batched and clear-all', jotai's atomFamily for 'dropping one member does not disturb its siblings', and query-core's utils.ts for 'exact identity versus a partial leading fragment'. Citations are usually where these runs lose recall; here they cost nothing.

16 shakedown calls carried the run. That is far above the tool's nominal budget share, but the anchor question is about a literal prefix-matching call against an object store, which is exactly the confirmable-text case shakedown is for.
what_went_wrong: The tldraw answer over-covered the sync-worker package: 12 of the 15 tldraw paths are non-gold neighbours (fileEffects, TLFileEffectProcessor, ogImageQueue, renderTokens, adminRoutes, thumbnailRender, types, config, worker, getThumbnailSnapshot) plus two store files. Once the right directory was found, the run returned most of it rather than discriminating inside it.
Each citation repo was answered with its whole neighbourhood rather than the one file: 4 query files for 1 gold, 5 redux-toolkit files for 2 gold. Only jotai was answered with exactly its gold file.

Cost. $32.70 for one case - 6.13M input tokens over 57 turns with caching disabled. Reaching rank-3 completeness took 56 tool calls and 105k tokens of tool output, and the input bill is that context re-sent every turn.
notes: precision@10 (0.30) is lower than precision@5 (0.60) because ranks 4-10 are all sync-worker neighbours. The gold is bimodal - a tight defect cluster at the top and three citations scattered at 17, 20/22 and 25 - so any cut below 25 loses citations.

retriever.surface: Opus 5 with the plumbline knowledge-graph MCP server, plus Bash and ToolSearch. No Read/Write/Edit/Grep/Glob/WebFetch/WebSearch/Task, and no subagents (subagent_stats.spawned = 0).
retriever.surface_pure_note: One Bash call was made. It ran `head -60` on the CLI's OWN saved overflow file for a plumbline stakeout result (~/.claude/projects/-private-tmp/<session>/tool-results/mcp-plumbline-stakeout-*.txt) - the arm re-reading its own MCP output after the CLI spilled it to disk. It touched no repository checkout, no golden.json and no sibling arm. Not a surface violation. ToolSearch (4 calls) loads MCP schemas and is exempt by convention.
retriever.isolation: kernel-enforced by sandbox-exec (profile at sandbox.sb, absolute subpaths). The whole benchmark tree is denied for read AND write, with mcp_plumbline.json the single re-opened literal path; ~/.claude/projects and history.jsonl are denied, so no earlier transcript - nor this run's own - was readable. cwd was /tmp, --setting-sources '' and --disable-slash-commands were set, so no CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks or auto-memory applied.
retriever.checkout_verified_note: run_prompt.txt instructs the arm not to verify checkouts or run gates; run.sh does not gate on git rev-parse. The arm reaches code only through the graph, so the pins that matter are the INDEX pins, and all four gold repos are indexed at exactly their pinned commits.
retriever.index_note: No gold repo is in either list: tldraw, redux-toolkit, jotai and query are all indexed at the pinned commit, so the index recall ceiling for this case is 1.0 - and the run reached it.

cost.launch: fresh isolated `claude -p` under sandbox-exec, --model claude-opus-5, --output-format json, --setting-sources '' --disable-slash-commands, --strict-mcp-config with ONLY the plumbline MCP server, --allowedTools Bash,ToolSearch + the 20 mcp__plumbline__* tools, --disallowedTools Read,Write,Edit,MultiEdit,NotebookEdit,Grep,Glob,WebFetch,WebSearch,Task,Agent,TodoWrite, --max-turns 120
cost.tokens_retrieved_note: approximated at 4 chars/token over the 56 tool_result blocks in the transcript
cost.prompt_caching: DISABLED (DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1). cache_creation and cache_read are both 0, confirming the setting took effect.
cost.cost_note: With caching off, every one of the 57 turns re-sends the full context at the full input rate: 6.13M input tokens x $5/Mtok = $30.63, plus 82.6k output x $25/Mtok = $2.07. The bill is context re-transmission, not retrieval - the 56 tool results are only ~105k tokens in total.
cost.cost_comparability_note: Cache-OFF run. Directly comparable to other arms run with DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1; NOT comparable to cache-on arms, whose USD figures are cached prices.

comparability.retrieval: clean: surface pure, kernel-enforced gold-blind isolation, no inherited context, no subagents, zero permission denials.
comparability.cost: clean: caching disabled, list-price basis, single isolated session.
